title: Fpqc-local equality of Picard classes determines their relative class
statement: Let $f:X\to B$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-picard-presheaf] such that $\mathcal O_T\to f_{T,*}\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism for every scheme $T$ over $B$. Let $L,L\prime\in\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$, and suppose the sieve of arrows $g:U\to T$ for which $g_X^*L=g_X^*L\prime$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Then the images of $L,L\prime$ in the relative Picard sheaf [def-pc-picard-functor] are equal.

source.place: Tags 0D27 (proof, kernel equals image) and 023T; exists_iso_tensorObj_of_toPicardFunctor_app_eq, ratio-cocycle proof generalized from fppf to fpqc

proof.text: Refine the fpqc equalizer sieve to an fpqc covering family. Its base change to X_T is fpqc. Form the tensor quotient K=L tensor dual(L-prime); it is trivial over the members of the base-changed covering. Compare its canonical descent datum with that of the pullback P of the base unit module. DescentCocycle.exists_iso_twist produces a ratio cocycle cX and an isomorphism with the twist of the descent datum of P. Universal triviality of the direct image identifies global functions on every X_Y with functions on Y, so cX.ofBaseChange gives a base cocycle cT whose pullback is cX. These are the already proved ratio-cocycle APIs in Picard.TwistedDescent.

Twist the canonical descent datum of the base unit by cT. Effective fpqc descent produces a quasi-coherent base module N; descent of invertibility makes N invertible. Compatibility of twisting with pullback identifies the descent data of f_T^*N and K. Fully faithful fpqc module descent yields f_T^*N isomorphic to K. Cancel the dual of L-prime to obtain L isomorphic to L-prime tensor f_T^*N.
Apply the reverse implication of toPicardFunctor_app_eq_iff: two invertible modules differing by a module pulled back from the base have equal images in the relative Picard sheaf.
